findings.failure_mode: Reading a widely-shared waitpoint (for example a manual token or datetime waitpoint many runs wait on) on the dedicated schema becomes slow and memory-heavy, and the request times out or the process runs out of memory.
findings.trigger_condition: A waitpoint has thousands of TaskRunWaitpoint edges and is read through the dedicated-schema hydrator with a nested taskRun select.
findings.amplifier: The edge query has no take/limit, and the run hydration then loads every distinct run row for those edges, with in-memory Maps built over all of them.
findings.blast_radius: Callers that fetch the waitpoint stall or fail for that waitpoint. Other waitpoints are unaffected, but the Postgres connection and Node heap are shared.

evidence.note: taskRunWaitpoint.findMany with only a waitpointId filter, no take.
All edge run ids are loaded into a Map with no cap.

findings.confidence_rationale: The code is unbounded, but I did not verify that real waitpoints reach very large fan-in on this path. boundedIn only chunks the IN list and does not cap the result.
findings.how_to_verify: Create 50k TaskRunWaitpoint rows for one waitpoint on the dedicated schema and hydrate it with a nested taskRun select. Memory and latency grow with the edge count.

findings.failure_mode: Fetching the completed waitpoints of a snapshot that completed a very large batch returns every link row in one query, and loads slowly on the run-continue path.
findings.trigger_condition: A snapshot has tens of thousands of completed-waitpoint links, for example a large batchTriggerAndWait.
findings.amplifier: The link read and the LEFT JOIN variant at 2255-2288 have no LIMIT, and the snapshot is read again on each continue or replay.
findings.blast_radius: Run continuation is slow for the affected runs only.

evidence.note: Legacy raw SELECT with no LIMIT.
Detector flagged the raw SELECT with no LIMIT.

findings.confidence_rationale: The result set is inherently the set of completed waitpoints, so it may be bounded by upstream batch-size limits that I did not check.
findings.how_to_verify: Complete a snapshot with 50k waitpoints and time findSnapshotCompletedWaitpointIds. If upstream caps batch size, reject this.

notes: Fix history is mostly features; the two fixes (366671e, 967dedc) address pool exhaustion and debounce state, and settlePendingUnit is a no-op here. I did not report 366671e as a recurring failure. I rejected S09 (delegateCache is a per-client memo of delegate wrappers) and S17 (the Maps at 284 and 365 are local to one call). The createExecutionSnapshot write path is idempotent via createMany skipDuplicates followed by a primary-key read. I did not check that the link inserts after the create are safe on replay.
